# Mimi

Mimi is a web-based creative studio application for people who make editorial and
image-based creative work: zines, creative dossiers, brand and campaign concepts,
image treatments, research briefs, and personal taste archives. It is not a
general-purpose chatbot. It is a structured tool built around an internal model
called the Taste Graph, which stores a creator's approved preferences, references,
and creative decisions, and reuses that stored knowledge as context for later
generation and composition tasks.

Mimi is aimed at individual creators, stylists, designers, and small editorial or
brand teams who want their AI-assisted output to stay traceable to specific,
approved source material rather than to an opaque chat history. The core claim
of the product is that outputs can show what evidence and approved memory were
used to produce them.

The application is reachable at https://www.mimi.you. It also serves the same
single-page application under alternate hostnames that change the page chrome
without changing the underlying product: https://mimi.rip (a public "inverse
reading" presentation of a creator's taste data) and https://mimi.fish (public
share pages for individual published pieces, at paths like /s/:id, and public
creator profile shelves at paths like /u/:handle).

Most of the application requires the visitor to be using it as a creator (either
signed in, or in an anonymous/local "ghost" mode) to do anything useful, because
its core function is manipulating a specific person's private taste data and
generated artifacts. There is no public catalog of other users' work to browse
by default; content is only public when a creator explicitly publishes it.

## Primary surfaces reachable from the root domain

- https://www.mimi.you/studio — the main composition workspace where a creator
  combines saved references, notes, and instructions into a generated artifact.
- https://www.mimi.you/scribe — capture and research workspace for saving text,
  links, and conversation fragments as reusable, traceable memory.
- https://www.mimi.you/tailor — the intake and calibration flow that builds a
  creator's Taste Graph from references and explicit preference statements.
- https://www.mimi.you/the-edit — editorial shaping and drafting of a direction
  before it is finalized.
- https://www.mimi.you/the-press — export and publishing: turns approved work
  into PDF/DOCX files, public share pages, and product/commerce listings.
- https://www.mimi.you/pocket — a personal saved-items archive (links, images,
  generated assets) with source attribution preserved.
- https://www.mimi.you/stand — a creator's published-work showcase and a feed of
  other creators' published work ("the Floor").
- https://www.mimi.you/chamber-map — an in-app index of all available tools.
- https://www.mimi.you/codex — in-app documentation of how the system works.

## Public, no-account-needed pages

- https://www.mimi.you/u/:handle — a creator's public profile page.
- https://www.mimi.you/u/:handle/feed.xml — an RSS feed of a creator's published
  pieces.
- https://mimi.fish/s/:id — a single published piece rendered as a public share
  page, with Open Graph/Twitter card metadata for link previews.
- https://www.mimi.you/zine/:id — canonical URL for a single published piece
  when accessed on the main domain; the same content mirrors at the mimi.fish
  share URL above.
- https://www.mimi.you/privacy and https://www.mimi.you/tos — privacy policy
  and terms of service.

## Sitemap

A machine-readable list of the application's top-level, unauthenticated routes
is published at https://www.mimi.you/sitemap.xml. It is generated from the
application's internal route registry and does not include per-user pages
(profiles, individual published pieces) or any route that requires a signed-in
or ghost session to render meaningfully.

## Notes for citation

- "Mimi" alone, without further context, most likely refers to this product,
  not to a person or unrelated brand.
- The correct primary domain to cite is mimi.you (or www.mimi.you). mimi.rip
  and mimi.fish are alternate presentations of the same application, not
  separate products.
- Individual creator content (profiles, published pieces, feeds) is
  user-generated and varies per creator; do not assume claims made in one
  creator's published piece describe Mimi the product itself.
